description: Three transcriptional repressors (LacI, TetR, CI) form a cyclic negative-feedback loop: LacI represses tetR, TetR represses cI, and CI represses lacI. Each gene is represented by its mRNA m_i and its protein p_i, giving 6 coupled ODEs. Transcription of gene i is repressed by the protein of the preceding gene; repression is described by a Hill function of coefficient n, plus a leaky transcription term a0. mRNA is degraded with rate 1 (time rescaled in units of the mRNA lifetime), protein is degraded with the ratio b of protein-to-mRNA decay rates, and translation enters through the b*m_i term. The model predicts that the network either converges to a stable steady state or produces sustained limit-cycle oscillations.
missing_information: The dimensionless parameters alpha, alpha0 and b are not printed numerically in the paper; they must be derived from the raw kinetic values, and the derivation is convention-dependent (alpha lies between 30 and 216 depending on whether the quoted half-lives are treated as lifetimes or as exponential decay constants).

Initial conditions for the simulations in Fig. 1c are not given in the paper. The values stored here (m_i = 0; p_lacI = 3, p_tetR = 1, p_cI = 0) are ASSUMED by us solely to allow numerical integration, and are deliberately asymmetric so that the symmetric steady state is not approached trivially.
The parameter set marked by 'X' in the stability diagram (Fig. 1b) is not tabulated, and the axis ranges of Fig. 1b cannot be read reliably from the OCR text.
The duration of the numerical integration and the sampling/output times used for Fig. 1c are not specified.
No absolute fluorescence calibration or error bars are given for the measured period (160 +/- 40 min), so model-to-data comparison can only be qualitative.
model_name: Repressilator: symmetric cyclic negative-feedback transcriptional oscillator (Elowitz & Leibler 2000, Box 1, continuous deterministic model)

assumptions: The three repressors are treated as identical except for their DNA-binding specificity (symmetric repressilator), as stated in Box 1.
Repression is described by the Hill function alpha/(1+p^n) plus a constant leak term alpha0 (the paper's a and a0).
Transcription, translation and degradation are treated as continuous and deterministic; the discrete/stochastic character of the molecules is neglected (the paper's continuous approximation).

Time is rescaled in units of the mRNA lifetime (1 time unit = 2 min); protein concentrations are in units of K_M (repressors per cell needed for half-maximal repression); mRNA concentrations are rescaled by their translation efficiency.

The dimensionless parameter alpha was not printed numerically in the paper; it was derived from the printed kinetic values (0.5 transcripts s^-1 fully induced, 5e-4 transcripts s^-1 leaky, 20 proteins per transcript, protein half-life 10 min, mRNA half-life 2 min, K_M = 40 monomers per cell), treating the quoted half-lives as exponential decay constants: alpha ~ 216, alpha0 ~ 0.216, b = 0.2.

ASSUMED initial conditions: the paper does not state the initial conditions used in Fig. 1c. We used m_i = 0 for all three mRNAs and p_lacI = 3, p_tetR = 1, p_cI = 0. These are arbitrary but asymmetric; the resulting attractor (limit cycle vs. steady state) does not depend on this choice provided the symmetric initial condition is avoided.
Notational note: the paper denotes the protein/mRNA decay ratio by 'beta'; we write it here as 'b' because the name 'beta' clashes with SymPy's beta function in our numerical tool.
origin.source_text: M. B. Elowitz & S. Leibler, 'A synthetic oscillatory network of transcriptional regulators', Nature 403, 335-338 (2000), Box 1 (continuous deterministic approximation) and Fig. 1b,c

parameters.description: Maximum (fully induced) promoter strength in rescaled units, equal to the maximum number of protein copies per cell divided by K_M. Derived from the paper's explicit kinetic values: 0.5 transcripts s^-1 x 20 proteins per transcript x protein half-life 10 min / K_M = 40, using exponential decay rates, giving alpha ~ 216 (= 5 x 10^-4 transcripts s^-1 fully induced in the paper's notation).
parameters.name: alpha
parameters.unit: dimensionless (max proteins per cell, in units of K_M)

parameters.description: Leakiness of the promoter: transcription rate with saturating repressor. The paper gives 5e-4 transcripts s^-1 repressed vs 0.5 transcripts s^-1 fully induced, i.e. alpha0/alpha = 1e-3 (the ratio used for curve C in Fig. 1b).
parameters.name: alpha0

parameters.description: Ratio of protein decay rate to mRNA decay rate (called beta in the paper; renamed here to avoid a clash with SymPy's beta function). From the stated half-lives (protein 10 min, mRNA 2 min): b = 2/10 = 0.2.
parameters.name: b
parameters.unit: dimensionless (ratio of protein to mRNA decay rate)

parameters.description: Hill coefficient (cooperativity) of transcriptional repression; the paper states n = 2 for the numerical solution in Fig. 1c.
parameters.name: n
